replies.author: @JobobJones-u5q
replies.text:
Um, not really. Notice how when the narrator is talking about bubbles rising from the water on Champagne Beach (around 7:55), the video is drone footage of a palm tree with the ocean in the background. Where's the footage of the tiny bubbles rising from the water that the narrator is describing? 

Though the narration is likely accurate, all of the video is stock footage and AI-enhanced content. 

Take a look at some of the channel's other videos; they all use the SAME format.

Ask yourself how a team of people could afford to travel to all of these islands and shoot, edit and produce videos that they then make available for free. 

Also, why are there no credits at the end of the videos listing everyone involved in the production? 
Answer: they are likely created by one or two people who have never been to the place the video is about, and are making these videos from footage shot by other people (some clips are obviously not from the place they claim to represent) and AI-enhanced video. 

Why are there no clips of people being interviewed, or anyone other than the narrator speaking? 

Answer: this is AI-generated content and/or stock footage that has been cobbled together to more or less match the narration.
